steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our security paper on optimized secure two-party computation protocols for the nonlinear activation functions used in RNNs (exponential, sigmoid, Tanh). Motivate privacy-preserving inference, explain the gap in existing 2PC work, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. AI, privacy concerns, and regulation motivating privacy-preserving DNNs
2. 2PC for private DNN inference and the remaining gaps
3. RNNs and their complex nonlinear activation functions
4. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Motivation
- AI evolving rapidly; health care, finance, manufacturing
- needs large amounts of data -> privacy problems, widespread concern
- EU General Data Privacy Regulation: personal data use requires data subject's consent
- motivates privacy-preserving DNN training and inference

2. 2PC
- SecureML (seminal): privacy-preserving DNN inference/training via secure two-party computation (2PC)
- 2PC: parties P_{1}, P_{2} jointly compute agreed function f on sensitive inputs x, y; nothing disclosed about inputs
- surge of 2PC-based private DNN inference works
- still a significant performance gap to practical applications
- 2PC inference supporting complex networks effectively/efficiently = open problem
- Table I: many works with deficiencies
- CrypTFlow2, Cheetah: private CNN inference (ResNet, DenseNet, MobileNet); only simple nonlinear functions (ReLU, Maxpool)

3. RNNs
- ChatGPT rising -> renewed spotlight on RNNs
- RNNs: sequential/time series data; NLP tasks (speech recognition, machine translation)
- complex nonlinear activations: exponential, sigmoid, Tanh
- few secure implementations, still not satisfactory

4. Contributions
- exponential: divide-and-conquer, mostly local computation; constant rounds, low communication, high-precision fixed-point; building block for sigmoid/Tanh
- sigmoid/Tanh: improve prior realizations; fewer building blocks via symmetry; fine-tune encoding of -x (with x\geq 0); saves cost and runtime
- comprehensive evaluation of secure exponential, sigmoid, Tanh; apply to full RNN inference

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been evolving quickly in recent years and it is used in many fields, such as health care, finance, manufacturing, and others. AI needs large amounts of data to learn, and as AI keeps evolving, a lot of privacy problems related to it have caused widespread concern. The European Union has set up the General Data Privacy Regulation, which says that using personal data requires the consent of the data subject. This has also motivated the development of privacy-preserving DNN training and inference.

SecureML was a seminal work that showed that privacy-preserving inference and training of DNN can be solved by secure two-party computation (2PC). 2PC lets the two parties, P_{1} and P_{2}, interactively compute an agreed function f on their sensitive inputs x and y, with strong guarantees that the interaction does not disclose any information about the sensitive inputs. Recently there have been a lot of 2PC-based works for privacy-preserving DNN inference. Even with all these efforts, there is still a big gap between privacy-preserving machine learning and practical applications in terms of performance. Also, 2PC secure inference protocols that support complex neural networks effectively and efficiently are still an open problem. As shown in Table I, many existing works have a wide range of deficiencies. CrypTFlow2 and Cheetah have been very successful in privacy-preserving CNN inference (e.g., ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet) using 2PC. But these networks only involve simple nonlinear functions like ReLU and Maxpool.

- RNNs
  - ChatGPT rising -> renewed spotlight on RNNs; sequential/time series data, NLP tasks (speech recognition, machine translation)
  - complex nonlinear activations: exponential, sigmoid, Tanh; few secure implementations, still not satisfactory
- Contributions
  - exponential: divide-and-conquer, mostly local; constant rounds, low communication, high-precision fixed-point; building block for sigmoid/Tanh
  - sigmoid/Tanh: fewer building blocks via symmetry; fine-tune encoding of -x (with x\geq 0)
  - comprehensive evaluation; full RNN inference

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been evolving quickly in recent years and it is used in many fields, such as health care, finance, manufacturing, and others. AI needs large amounts of data to learn, and as AI keeps evolving, a lot of privacy problems related to it have caused widespread concern. The European Union has set up the General Data Privacy Regulation, which says that using personal data requires the consent of the data subject. This has also motivated the development of privacy-preserving DNN training and inference.

SecureML was a seminal work that showed that privacy-preserving inference and training of DNN can be solved by secure two-party computation (2PC). 2PC lets the two parties, P_{1} and P_{2}, interactively compute an agreed function f on their sensitive inputs x and y, with strong guarantees that the interaction does not disclose any information about the sensitive inputs. Recently there have been a lot of 2PC-based works for privacy-preserving DNN inference. Even with all these efforts, there is still a big gap between privacy-preserving machine learning and practical applications in terms of performance. Also, 2PC secure inference protocols that support complex neural networks effectively and efficiently are still an open problem. As shown in Table I, many existing works have a wide range of deficiencies. CrypTFlow2 and Cheetah have been very successful in privacy-preserving CNN inference (e.g., ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet) using 2PC. But these networks only involve simple nonlinear functions like ReLU and Maxpool.

With ChatGPT rising, a popular language model that generates human-like responses in natural language conversations, the spotlight is on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) again. RNNs are neural networks that can process sequential or time series data and they are commonly used for natural language processing tasks like speech recognition and machine translation. These networks use a lot of nonlinear activation functions that are more complex, such as exponential, sigmoid, and Tanh functions. Unfortunately only a few works have given secure implementations of these nonlinear functions, and those works are still not satisfactory.

These demands lead us to further optimize the 2PC protocols for nonlinear activation functions. Our contributions are as follows:

- We propose a new 2PC implementation of the exponential function that uses a divide-and-conquer strategy, with most of the computations done locally. The protocol needs only a constant number of rounds and low communication in high-precision fixed-point operations. It is an efficiency building block for the 2PC implementation of sigmoid and Tanh.
- We improve the existing realizations of sigmoid and Tanh from prior work by using the symmetry of the functions to reduce 2PC building blocks. We also reduce the building blocks further by fine-tuning the encoding of -x (with x\geq 0). This saves both cost and runtime.
- Finally, we did a comprehensive evaluation of our secure exponential, sigmoid, and Tanh functions. We also apply our secure sigmoid and Tanh protocol to an entire process of RNN inference, which further shows our improvements.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving in recent years and is being used in a variety of fields, including health care, finance, manufacturing, and beyond. AI requires large amounts of data for learning, and as AI continues to evolve, numerous privacy problems related to it have aroused widespread concern. The European Union has set up the General Data Privacy Regulation [1], which specifies that the utilization of personal data requires the consent of the data subject. It has also motivated the development of privacy-preserving DNN training and inference.

The seminal work of SecureML [2] demonstrated that privacy-preserving inference and training of DNN can be resolved by secure two-party computation (2PC). 2PC [3,4] allows the two parties, P_{1} and P_{2}, to interactively compute an agreed function f on their sensitive inputs x and y, with strong guarantees that the interaction discloses no information about the sensitive inputs. There has recently been a surge of 2PC-based works for privacy-preserving DNN inference [5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12]. Despite these efforts, a significant performance gap remains from privacy-preserving machine learning to practical applications. Also, 2PC secure inference protocols that support complex neural networks effectively and efficiently remain an open problem. As shown in Table I, many existing works suffer from a wide range of deficiencies. CrypTFlow2 [7] and Cheetah [11] have achieved great success in privacy-preserving CNN inference (e.g., ResNet [13], DenseNet [14], and MobileNet [15]) through 2PC. However, these networks only involve simple nonlinear functions such as ReLU and Maxpool.

With the rise of ChatGPT, a popular language model that generates human-like responses in natural language conversations, the spotlight has once again turned towards Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). RNNs are neural networks that can process sequential or time series data and are commonly used for natural language processing tasks such as speech recognition and machine translation. These networks make extensive use of more complex nonlinear activation functions, such as exponential, sigmoid, and Tanh functions. Unfortunately, only a few works have provided secure implementations of these nonlinear functions [2,5,16], and those works are still not satisfactory.

These demands drive us to further optimize the 2PC protocols for nonlinear activation functions. The contributions of this paper are summarized as follows:

- We propose a novel 2PC implementation of the exponential function using a divide-and-conquer strategy, with most of the computations executed locally. The proposed protocol requires only a constant number of rounds and low communication in high-precision fixed-point operations. It provides an efficiency building block for the 2PC implementation of sigmoid and Tanh.
- We improve the existing realizations of sigmoid and Tanh from [10] by reducing 2PC building blocks through the symmetry of the functions. In addition, we further reduce the building blocks by fine-tuning the encoding of -x (with x\geq 0). This saves both cost and runtime.
- Finally, we conducted a comprehensive evaluation of our secure exponential, sigmoid, and Tanh functions. We also apply our secure sigmoid and Tanh protocol to an entire process of RNN inference, which further demonstrates our improvements.
